findings.title: Public findMany method deleted without migration
findings.body: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts previously exposed findMany(findManyArgs) that applied authorization and filter conditions via a Prisma where clause. This PR deletes that method and only exposes getBaseConditions() returning Prisma.Sql for manual $queryRaw use. Any existing caller that still calls service.findMany() will fail at compile time / throw TypeError: service.findMany is not a function at runtime. Deleting a public service method in the same change that converts internals to raw SQL is a breaking contract change and requires updating all call sites in the same PR.

findings.title: toEqual on Prisma.Sql compares template segmentation, not SQL semantics
findings.body: The test at packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:295 expects team/org/combined conditions with expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...flat template...`). The service builds the same SQL text via nested interpolation, e.g. Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR (${condition})` and Prisma.sql`(${acc}) AND (${condition})` in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, buildTeamAuthorizationCondition and buildFilterConditions. Prisma.Sql stores strings[] plus values[]; nested Sql values are flattened by splicing, so the resulting strings[] segmentation differs from a hand-written flat template even when the final SQL text and bound values are identical. toEqual therefore fails on false negatives, making the authorization/filter tests red while the query is semantically correct. Tests should compare rendered SQL plus values or execute the query instead of deep-equaling Sql objects.

findings.title: Org-scope expectation assumes deterministic DB row order
findings.body: The org-scope test at packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:333 expects teamIds = [org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id] and userIds = [user.id, user2.id, user3.id] in that exact order. The service builds those arrays from TeamRepository.findAllByParentId and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds with no ORDER BY. Database return order is undefined, so the ANY(...) arrays can come back in any order. The test will flake or fail when Postgres returns rows in a different order even though authorization is correct. The test must sort both expected and actual arrays or assert order-insensitively.
